qs.q: What figures does the paper give for data center electricity use and its projection, and for the energy used to train GPT-4?
qs.a: About 415 TWh in 2024 (1.5% of worldwide electricity), projected to exceed 945 TWh by 2030 with 30% annual growth in accelerated servers (IEA); GPT-4 training between 51,772 and 62,318 MWh

qs.q: What bandwidth figures are given for NVLink and InfiniBand, in what units, and does the paper compare the two?
qs.a: NVLink up to 900 GB/s per GPU in Blackwell (gigabytes per second, intra-node); InfiniBand NDR-class up to 800 Gb/s (gigabits per second), latency below one microsecond. The units differ (GB/s vs Gb/s) and the paper does not rank one above the other; they serve intra-node vs inter-node links

qs.q: By how much did spatio-temporal workload migration reduce carbon emissions of AI training, relative to what?
qs.a: 5% to 10% relative to static geographic placement, from cited recent work

qs.q: What energy or compute reduction does the paper attribute to quantization, and do the text and the table state the same thing?
qs.a: Text: per-inference energy falls by roughly a factor of two to four versus full precision. Table 3 states a 2x to 4x reduction in memory and compute. So the text says energy, the table says memory and compute

qs.q: Does the paper report its own measurements or experiments showing that distributed architectures cut energy or emissions?
qs.a: No. It is an argument built on cited sources and general reasoning; the quantified claims come from cited work (for example 5-10% carbon reduction, 2-4x quantization), and no original experiment or dataset is presented

qs.q: What evidence does the paper give for the claim that well-tuned 3D hybrid parallelism scales near-linearly?
qs.a: It states that empirical deployments have shown near-linear scaling efficiency, so energy per unit of training progress stays about constant as the cluster grows, with a single citation and no numbers or named deployment

qs.q: Does the paper contain a limitations section or quantify the energy cost of the distributed approaches it proposes?
qs.a: No limitations section. It mentions overheads (consensus and coordination traffic, BFT, CAP trade-offs) but gives no figure for them, and the conclusion calls distributed infrastructure the most credible foundation

qs.q: What does the paper conclude about hardware efficiency improvements, and why?
qs.a: They are useful but cannot close the gap alone: by Jevons' paradox cheaper computation raises demand faster than per-unit savings, so total consumption rises; hence a structural shift to distributed systems is argued

qs.q: What fraction of training energy is spent on Raft consensus traffic?
qs.a: NOT STATED. Consensus overhead is described as pure coordination overhead with no measured share

qs.q: What share of training time are GPUs idle in large parameter-server deployments?
qs.a: NOT STATED. The paper says only that the idle fraction is high enough to be a meaningful efficiency loss, without a number
